scope: Only four per-trail originally scored effects and number of matched trail-year-area groups. No original Event/Occurrence open or plant-level refit.
question: Can aggregation level conceal/reverse native-to-alien spatial-gradient direction in observational island trail plant communities, and is the log-ratio direction the same as absolute native-richness direction?

calculations.primary_reference: Original v1.295 equal-independent-trail average remains sole frozen primary point estimate; never replace by more favorable pooled result
calculations.sensitivity1: Equal island weight: average Terceira mean across its 3 trails and Sao Miguel 1-trail mean, purely descriptive, NOT independent island replication
calculations.sensitivity2: Group-count-weighted trail effect: weighted average over matched area-year group count (n=1,7,6,3); treats 17 repeated within-trail area groups as potential units and is intentionally a NONINDEPENDENT descriptive sensitivity, not a valid new primary
calculations.individual_patterns: For each original trail report whether relative native/alien log ratio is positive vs negative, whether absolute native species richness is positive vs negative, and whether alien species richness changes correspondingly
calculations.heterogeneity: Report per-island trail range, number of positive and negative signs and bounded min-max of original 4 trail effects; do not fit model or calculate significance
calculations.weighting_direction: Report signed directions under all 3 weighting schemes and whether sign reverses. A positive nonindependent pooled average must NOT rescue negative/near-zero original primary.

evidence_class: posthoc source-free arithmetic on already frozen observational trail aggregates, no new independent ecological confirmation
